paper_metadata.title: Microcracking in multipass weld metal of alloy 690 Part 2 – Microcracking mechanism in reheated weld metal
paper_metadata.journal: Science and Technology of Welding and Joining

evidence.quote: The Ni base superalloy 690 exhibits a high hot cracking susceptibility during multipass welding.
A fully austenitic alloy, Invar, was also employed for comparison with alloy 690 in the investigation of local deformability.

The base metal used in the present work is a commercial alloy 690. Three types of ﬁller metal with varying contents of impurity elements were used. The chemical compositions of the base metal and ﬁller metals are given in Table 1.
Three types of ﬁller metal with varying contents of impurity elements were used. ... The principal variables in the ﬁller metals were mainly P and S content.

The Invar alloy possesses a high microcracking (ductility dip cracking) susceptibility, and is typical in having a cracking temperature range located at intermediate temperature (750–1200 K).8,9 The chemical composition of the Invar alloy used is also presented in Table 1.

The test specimens for evaluating the microcracking susceptibility were manufactured by single pass GTA welding (4 mm thick plate with 90 u single V groove, 0 .5 mm root face) using the above ﬁller metals under the following welding conditions: arc current 160 A, arc voltage 14 V, and welding speed 1 .67 mm s 21.

evidence.section: Hot ductility of reheated weld metal
evidence.quote: The reduction of area of the weld metal FF1 decreases to less than about 20% at 1373 K; however, those of FF3 and FF5 recover slightly in the temperature range above 1500 K.
The computer simulation of microsegregation suggested that the deterioration of hot ductility is caused by the grain boundary segregation of impurity elements during the multiple thermal cycling.

The ductility dip cracking in the reheated weld metal resulted predominantly from the embrittlement of grain boundaries due to the imbalance between intergranular strength and intragranular strength at high temperature.
